events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Northeastern Sumter County in central Florida...

* WHEN...Until 500 PM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 350 PM EDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain due to thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly in the advisory area. Between 2 and 3
inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1 inch are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Wildwood, Lake Panasoffkee, Coleman, Sumterville and Adamsville.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Burlington, NJ; Mercer, NJ; Bucks, PA
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
At 345 PM EDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches have fallen with the heavy
rainfall that moved through the area this afternoon. There have also
been multiple reports of road flooding. The heaviest rain has
tapered off at this time but it will still take some time for the
waters to fully recede so the Flash Flood Warning remains in effect.
There may also be some additional showers moving through the area
through early this evening.



HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by heavy rain.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets, and underpasses as well as other
drainage and low lying areas.

Some locations that may experience flash flooding include...
Trenton, Ewing, Florence, Burlington, Bristol, Bordentown,
Yardley, Tullytown, Langhorne, Pemberton, Wrightstown and Columbus.

This includes the following highways...
Interstate 295 in New Jersey between mile markers 48 and 66.
New Jersey Turnpike between exits 6 and 7A.
Interstate 195 in New Jersey between mile markers 0 and 5.
Pennsylvania Turnpike between mile markers 356 and 359.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Hunterdon, NJ; Warren, NJ; Bucks, PA
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
FFWPHI

The National Weather Service in Mount Holly has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Hunterdon County in northwestern New Jersey...
Southwestern Warren County in northwestern New Jersey...
North Central Bucks County in southeastern Pennsylvania...

* Until 730 PM EDT.

* At 333 PM EDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
thunderstorms producing heavy rain just beginning to move into the
warned area. These storms have a history of producing 1 to 2
inches of rainfall within an hour and causing flash flooding.
Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets, and underpasses as well as other
drainage and low lying areas.

* Some locations that may experience flash flooding include...
Easton, Flemington, High Bridge, Clinton, Alpha, Glen Gardner,
Ferndale, Hampton, Frenchtown, Lebanon, Milford and Califon.

This includes Interstate 78 in New Jersey between mile markers 0 and
23.
